    **Statement.** Let n=3, N=8, Theta_3^down = {theta_i >= 4/15}, gauge (rho,lambda)=(40,20), ledgers per statement lock (parity candidate (M,D,L) = (3m+2, 0, 4)). The parity policy dominates (weak in (M,D,L), strict in M) the complete randomized variable-length no-recovery prefix hull for every theta in Theta_3^down iff 1 <= m <= 16. m_crit(3) = 16.
    
    **Proof.**
    (a) *No-message face.* P_{0,m}(theta) = 2^{-3} sum_B theta(B)^m is symmetric convex, hence Schur-convex, maximized at the majorization-maximal vertex (7,4,4)/15. gamma_{0,m} = 39 - 2m - 40 P_{0,m} at the vertex is positive for m <= 16 (gamma_{0,16} = 845049722020265693/437893890380859375 ~= +1.929805) and negative at m=17 (gamma_{0,17} = -22519522704133297/437893890380859375 ~= -0.051427). Monotonicity on 10 <= m <= 16 via the integer certificates 20 m^m < (m+1)^{m+1} (same z^m(1-z) bound as Cont-2). At m=17 failure holds at EVERY theta: gamma is maximized where P is minimized (uniform law), gamma_{0,17}(unif) = -218455/14348907 < 0; for m >= 18 the universal P >= 1/8 gives gamma <= 34 - 2m <= -2. const cr=await zero.fs.compound('read',{path:'/tmp/w7_sol_p1_check.py'});
const checker=cr.text;
const report=String.raw`# RADC Wave-7 P1: exact general-(n\) sequential full-prefix phase

**Artifact ID:** \(\mathrm{W7\mbox{-}SOL\mbox{-}SEQ\mbox{-}DOWN\mbox{-}STAIRCASE}\)  
**Verdict:** PROVED and independently EC-attested under the locked formal ledger.  
**Scope:** \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\), \((\rho,\lambda)=(40,20)\), sequential, no-recovery, every variable-length binary prefix policy, arbitrary randomization, joint failure distortion.

> Encoding note: occurrences of the control glyph before TeX delimiters in this draft are not semantic and are removed in the final write below.

## 0. Executive result: the 16/18/19 conflict is resolved

Let

\[
\Theta_n^\downarrow=\left\{\theta\in\Delta_{n-1}:\theta_i\ge {4\over5n}\right\},
\qquad
v_n={1\over5n}(n+4,4,\ldots,4).
\]

For \(n\ge2\), the parity/complement policy has the locked ledger

\[
(M_{\rm par},D_{\rm par},L_{\rm par})=(3m+2,0,4).
\]

It weakly improves every coordinate and strictly improves at least one coordinate, uniformly over \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\), against the **complete randomized variable-length no-recovery prefix hull**, exactly for

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal D_n=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&n=2,\\
\{1,\ldots,16\},&n=3,\\
\{1,\ldots,18\},&n=4,5,\\
\{1,\ldots,19\},&n\ge6.
\end{cases}}
\]

With the convention \(\max\varnothing=0\),

\[
\boxed{m_{\rm crit}(2)=0,\quad m_{\rm crit}(3)=16,\quad
m_{\rm crit}(4)=m_{\rm crit}(5)=18,\quad
m_{\rm crit}(n)=19\ (n\ge6).}
\]

Thus **16** is the \(n=3\) heavy-vertex no-message cutoff, **18** is the \(n=4,5\) cutoff, and **19** is the stable all-\(n\ge6\) tail. The full phase is empty at \(n=2\) because latency, not memory, kills parity.

## 1. Status/index

| W7 ID | Result | Evidence | Ambition |
|---|---|---|---|
| W7-SOL-OCCUPANCY-PROJECTION | \(r\)-leaf success projection and exact no-message moment | PI\|DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-PREFIX-SPECTRUM-N | exact closed \(C_N(r)\), checked against root-split DP through \(N=64\) | DR\|EC | [S] |
| W7-SOL-BLOCK-FANO-BARRIER | every nontrivial tree excluded for \(n\ge4,2\le m\le19\) | DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-Q3-FULLPREFIX | every nontrivial Q3 tree excluded for \(3\le m\le16\), with exact small-\(m\) splice | PI\|DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-SEQ-DOWN-STAIRCASE | complete randomized-hull phase above | PI\|DR\|EC | [M] |
| W7-SOL-P1-ATTEST | independent exact checker embedded in §8 | EC | [S] |

Tags: PI = inherited locked input; DR = deductive reconstruction; EC = exact computation; BE = bounded experiment; SB = speculative bridge. No BE or SB is used in the theorem.

## 2. Statement lock

Let \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)\), and let \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}\theta\), independent of \(X\). Conditioned on all policy randomness, a no-recovery encoder emits before demands a binary prefix transcript \(Z\) whose \(r\) nonempty leaves \(A_j\) partition the \(N=2^n\) source words. If leaf \(j\) has depth \(d_j\),

\[
\ell={1\over N}\sum_{j=1}^r |A_j|d_j.
\]

The decoder sees no correctness oracle or source-dependent feedback after the transcript. Put

\[
P_T=\Pr[\widehat X_{S_t}=X_{S_t}\ \forall t\le m],\qquad e_T=1-P_T.
\]

The locked baseline ledger is

\[
M_T=(m+1)(1+\ell)+40e_T,
\quad L_T=1+\ell+c_{\rm comp}+20e_T,
\quad D_T=e_T,
\quad c_{\rm comp}\ge0.
\]

Dominance means weak in \((M,D,L)\) with at least one strict coordinate. All randomized claims condition on the complete seed and then average.

## 3. Occupancy projection and no-message face

Put \(Q_m=\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}\) and \(K_m=|Q_m|\).

### Lemma W7-SOL-OCCUPANCY-PROJECTION

For every deterministic \(r\)-leaf realization,

\[
\boxed{P_T\le \mathbb E_\theta\min\{1,r2^{-K_m}\}.}\tag{3.1}
\]

**Proof.** Fix the demand sequence, a leaf, and decoder randomness. If \(K_m=k\), consistent answers fix the source bits on the \(k\) visited coordinates, leaving at most \(2^{n-k}\) compatible cube words per leaf; inconsistent repeated answers leave none. Across \(r\) leaves there are at most \(\min(2^n,r2^{n-k})\) successful words. Uniform \(X\) gives (3.1). ∎

For \(r=1\), a fixed prototype attains equality:

\[
\boxed{P_{0,m}(\theta)=\mathbb E_\theta 2^{-K_m}
=2^{-n}\sum_{B\subseteq[n]}\theta(B)^m.}\tag{3.2}
\]

The function in (3.2) is symmetric and convex, hence Schur-convex. Its maximum on \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\) is attained at \(v_n\). Writing \(p_{n,m}=P_{0,m}(v_n)\),

\[
\boxed{
p_{n,m}={1\over2^n(5n)^m}
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}{n-1\choose k}
\left[(n+4+4k)^m+(4k)^m\right].}
\tag{3.3}
\]

The worst-class no-message memory gap is

\[
\boxed{G_0(n,m)=40(1-p_{n,m})-(2m+1).}\tag{3.4}
\]

For \(m\ge10\),

\[
p_{n,m}-p_{n,m+1}=\mathbb E[Z^m(1-Z)]
\le {m^m\over(m+1)^{m+1}}<{1\over20},
\tag{3.5}
\]

where the strict inequality is the integer certificate

\[
\boxed{20m^m<(m+1)^{m+1}.}\tag{3.6}
\]

Hence \(G_0(n,m)>G_0(n,m+1)\) on the relevant tail.

### Exact endpoint signs

| \(n\) | last positive \(m\) | \(G_0\) there | first negative \(m\) | \(G_0\) there |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 16 | \(845049722020265693/437893890380859375\) | 17 | \(-22519522704133297/437893890380859375\) |
| 4 | 18 | \(277615146191/762939453125\) | 19 | \(-1227337666073/762939453125\) |
| 5 | 18 | \(887975035189461090631639/582076609134674072265625\) | 19 | \(-254541365995396231447867/582076609134674072265625\) |
| 6 | 19 | \(2975301311635846283/19705225067138671875\) | 20 | \(-2684852348710641308821/1477891880035400390625\) |

### Exact all-\(n\) tail, not bounded extrapolation

Pad \(v_n\) by a zero. Its first \(k\le n\) ordered partial sums are

\[
{1\over5}+{4k\over5n}
>
{1\over5}+{4k\over5(n+1)},
\tag{3.7}
\]

those of \(v_{n+1}\). Thus \((v_n,0)\succ v_{n+1}\). Schur-convexity gives

\[
p_{n,m}\ge p_{n+1,m},\qquad G_0(n,m)\le G_0(n+1,m).
\tag{3.8}
\]

The exact \(n=6\) signs therefore prove \(G_0(n,m)>0\) for every \(n\ge6,m\le19\). This is the required symbolic all-\(n\) tail; no finite extrapolation is used.

## 4. Exact prefix spectrum

Let \(C_N(r)\) be the minimum unnormalized external path length over \(r\) nonempty prefix leaves and \(N\) equiprobable source states. Define

\[
U(s)=s(a+2)-2^{a+1},\qquad a=\lfloor\log_2s\rfloor,
\quad U(1)=0.
\tag{4.1}
\]

For \(1\le d\le\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor\), put

\[
k=2^d,
\quad q=\left\lfloor{r-1\over k-1}\right\rfloor,
\quad b=(r-1)-(k-1)q,
\]

\[
V_d(r)=(k-1-b)U(q)+bU(q+1).
\tag{4.2}
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{C_N(1)=0,
\qquad C_N(r)=\min_{1\le d\le\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor}\left[Nd+V_d(r)\right].}
\tag{4.3}
\]

**Proof.** For fixed depths, put one source in every leaf and all \(N-r\) extra sources in a minimum-depth leaf. If the minimum leaf depth is \(d\), the \(2^d\) level-\(d\) nodes root nonempty subtrees, at least one containing one final leaf. The cost is \(Nd+\sum_iU(r_i)\), \(\sum r_i=r\), one \(r_i=1\). Discrete convexity of \(U\) makes the other \(r-1\) leaves as equal as possible, yielding (4.2). The corresponding complete subtrees attain the bound. ∎

The checker verifies (4.3) against an independent root-split DP for every \(1\le r\le N\le64\). In particular,

\[
C_{16}=(0,16,18,21,24,28,32,36,40,45,50,53,56,60,62,64).
\tag{4.4}
\]

## 5. Every nontrivial tree

### 5.1 The \(n=3\) projection certificate

For \(N=8\), define

\[
c_r={C_8(r)\over8},
\quad u_r=\mathbb E_{v_3}\min\{1,r2^{-K_m}\},
\quad b_r=1-u_r.
\]

By (3.1) and (4.3), every \(r\)-leaf tree obeys

\[
M_T-(3m+2)\ge (m+1)c_r-(2m+1)+40b_r.
\tag{5.1}
\]

Equivalently, the exact projection-length threshold is

\[
\rho_{\rm PL}(3,m)=

let report=String.raw`# RADC Wave-7 P1: exact general-\(n\) sequential full-prefix phase

**Artifact ID:** \(\mathrm{W7\mbox{-}SOL\mbox{-}SEQ\mbox{-}DOWN\mbox{-}STAIRCASE}\)  
**Verdict:** PROVED and independently EC-attested under the locked formal ledger.  
**Scope:** \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\), \((\rho,\lambda)=(40,20)\), sequential, no-recovery, every variable-length binary prefix policy, arbitrary randomization, joint failure distortion.

## 0. Executive result: the 16/18/19 conflict is resolved

Let

\[
\Theta_n^\downarrow=\left\{\theta\in\Delta_{n-1}:\theta_i\ge {4\over5n}\right\},
\qquad
v_n={1\over5n}(n+4,4,\ldots,4).
\]

For \(n\ge2\), the parity/complement policy has the locked ledger

\[
(M_{\rm par},D_{\rm par},L_{\rm par})=(3m+2,0,4).
\]

It weakly improves every coordinate and strictly improves at least one coordinate, uniformly over \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\), against the **complete randomized variable-length no-recovery prefix hull**, exactly for

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal D_n=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&n=2,\\
\{1,\ldots,16\},&n=3,\\
\{1,\ldots,18\},&n=4,5,\\
\{1,\ldots,19\},&n\ge6.
\end{cases}}
\]

With \(\max\varnothing=0\),

\[
\boxed{m_{\rm crit}(2)=0,\quad m_{\rm crit}(3)=16,\quad
m_{\rm crit}(4)=m_{\rm crit}(5)=18,\quad
m_{\rm crit}(n)=19\ (n\ge6).}
\]

Thus **16** is the \(n=3\) heavy-vertex no-message cutoff, **18** is the \(n=4,5\) cutoff, and **19** is the stable all-\(n\ge6\) tail. The full phase is empty at \(n=2\) because latency, not memory, kills parity.

## 1. Status/index

|---|---|---|---|
| W7-SOL-OCCUPANCY-PROJECTION | \(r\)-leaf success projection and exact no-message moment | PI\|DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-PREFIX-SPECTRUM-N | exact closed \(C_N(r)\), checked against root-split DP through \(N=64\) | DR\|EC | [S] |
| W7-SOL-BLOCK-FANO-BARRIER | every nontrivial tree excluded for \(n\ge4,2\le m\le19\) | DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-Q3-FULLPREFIX | every nontrivial Q3 tree excluded for \(3\le m\le16\), with exact small-\(m\) splice | PI\|DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-SEQ-DOWN-STAIRCASE | complete randomized-hull phase above | PI\|DR\|EC | [M] |
| W7-SOL-P1-ATTEST | independent exact checker embedded in §8 | EC | [S] |

Tags: PI = inherited locked input; DR = deductive reconstruction; EC = exact computation; BE = bounded experiment; SB = speculative bridge. No BE or SB is used in the theorem.

## 2. Statement lock

Let \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)\), and let \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}\theta\), independent of \(X\). Conditioned on all policy randomness, a no-recovery encoder emits before demands a binary prefix transcript \(Z\) whose \(r\) nonempty leaves \(A_j\) partition the \(N=2^n\) source words. If leaf \(j\) has depth \(d_j\),

\[
\ell={1\over N}\sum_{j=1}^r |A_j|d_j.
\]

The decoder sees no correctness oracle or source-dependent feedback after the transcript. Put

\[
P_T=\Pr[\widehat X_{S_t}=X_{S_t}\ \forall t\le m],\qquad e_T=1-P_T.
\]

The locked baseline ledger is

\[
M_T=(m+1)(1+\ell)+40e_T,
\quad L_T=1+\ell+c_{\rm comp}+20e_T,
\quad D_T=e_T,
\quad c_{\rm comp}\ge0.
\]

Dominance means weak in \((M,D,L)\) with at least one strict coordinate. Randomized claims condition on the complete seed and average.

## 3. Occupancy projection and no-message face

Put \(Q_m=\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}\), \(K_m=|Q_m|\).

### W7-SOL-OCCUPANCY-PROJECTION

For every deterministic \(r\)-leaf realization,

\[
\boxed{P_T\le \mathbb E_\theta\min\{1,r2^{-K_m}\}.}\tag{3.1}
\]

**Proof.** Fix the demand sequence, a leaf, and decoder randomness. If \(K_m=k\), consistent answers fix the source bits on the \(k\) visited coordinates, leaving at most \(2^{n-k}\) compatible cube words per leaf; inconsistent repeated answers leave none. Across \(r\) leaves there are at most \(\min(2^n,r2^{n-k})\) successful words. Uniform \(X\) gives (3.1). ∎

For \(r=1\), a fixed prototype attains equality:

\[
\boxed{P_{0,m}(\theta)=\mathbb E_\theta 2^{-K_m}
=2^{-n}\sum_{B\subseteq[n]}\theta(B)^m.}\tag{3.2}
\]

This function is symmetric and convex, hence Schur-convex. Its maximum on \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\) is attained at \(v_n\). Writing \(p_{n,m}=P_{0,m}(v_n)\),

\[
\boxed{
p_{n,m}={1\over2^n(5n)^m}
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}{n-1\choose k}
\left[(n+4+4k)^m+(4k)^m\right].}
\tag{3.3}
\]

The worst-class no-message memory gap is

\[
\boxed{G_0(n,m)=40(1-p_{n,m})-(2m+1).}\tag{3.4}
\]

For \(m\ge10\),

\[
p_{n,m}-p_{n,m+1}=\mathbb E[Z^m(1-Z)]
\le {m^m\over(m+1)^{m+1}}<{1\over20},
\tag{3.5}
\]

where the strict integer certificate is

\[
\boxed{20m^m<(m+1)^{m+1}.}\tag{3.6}
\]

Hence \(G_0(n,m)>G_0(n,m+1)\) on the relevant tail.

### Exact endpoint signs

|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 16 | \(845049722020265693/437893890380859375\) | 17 | \(-22519522704133297/437893890380859375\) |
| 4 | 18 | \(277615146191/762939453125\) | 19 | \(-1227337666073/762939453125\) |
| 5 | 18 | \(887975035189461090631639/582076609134674072265625\) | 19 | \(-254541365995396231447867/582076609134674072265625\) |

### Exact all-\(n\) tail

Pad \(v_n\) by a zero. Its first \(k\le n\) ordered partial sums satisfy

\[
{1\over5}+{4k\over5n}
>
{1\over5}+{4k\over5(n+1)},
\tag{3.7}
\]

those of \(v_{n+1}\). Thus \((v_n,0)\succ v_{n+1}\). Schur-convexity gives

\[
p_{n,m}\ge p_{n+1,m},\qquad G_0(n,m)\le G_0(n+1,m).
\tag{3.8}
\]

The exact \(n=6\) signs therefore prove \(G_0(n,m)>0\) for every \(n\ge6,m\le19\). This is symbolic all-\(n\) closure, not finite extrapolation.

## 4. Exact prefix spectrum

Let \(C_N(r)\) be the minimum unnormalized external path length over \(r\) nonempty prefix leaves and \(N\) equiprobable source states. Define

\[
U(s)=s(a+2)-2^{a+1},\qquad a=\lfloor\log_2s\rfloor,
\quad U(1)=0.
\tag{4.1}
\]

For \(1\le d\le\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor\), put

\[
k=2^d,
\quad q=\left\lfloor{r-1\over k-1}\right\rfloor,
\quad b=(r-1)-(k-1)q,
\]

\[
V_d(r)=(k-1-b)U(q)+bU(q+1).
\tag{4.2}
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{C_N(1)=0,
\qquad C_N(r)=\min_{1\le d\le\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor}\left[Nd+V_d(r)\right].}
\tag{4.3}
\]

**Proof.** For fixed depths, put one source in every leaf and all \(N-r\) extras in a minimum-depth leaf. If the minimum depth is \(d\), the \(2^d\) level-\(d\) nodes root nonempty subtrees and at least one contains one final leaf. The cost is \(Nd+\sum_iU(r_i)\), \(\sum r_i=r\), one \(r_i=1\). Discrete convexity of \(U\) makes the other \(r-1\) leaves as equal as possible, yielding (4.2); complete subtrees attain it. ∎

The checker verifies (4.3) against an independent root-split DP for every \(1\le r\le N\le64\). In particular,

\[
C_{16}=(0,16,18,21,24,28,32,36,40,45,50,53,56,60,62,64).
\tag{4.4}
\]

## 5. Every nontrivial tree

### 5.1 The \(n=3\) projection certificate

For \(N=8\), define

\[
c_r={C_8(r)\over8},
\quad u_r=\mathbb E_{v_3}\min\{1,r2^{-K_m}\},
\quad b_r=1-u_r.
\]

By (3.1) and (4.3), every \(r\)-leaf tree obeys

\[
M_T-(3m+2)\ge (m+1)c_r-(2m+1)+40b_r.
\tag{5.1}
\]

The exact threshold is

\[
\rho_{\rm PL}(3,m)=
\max_{1\le r\le8}
{[2m+1-(m+1)c_r]_+\over b_r}.
\tag{5.2}
\]

Exact occupancy recurrence gives \(\rho_{\rm PL}(3,m)<40\) for \(3\le m\le16\), with

\[
\boxed{\rho_{\rm PL}(3,16)=
{144504983825683593750\over3823887026147156267}
\approx37.790076651737.}
\tag{5.3}
\]

For \(m=1,2\), first-answer reduction gives

\[
M_T\ge {m+1\over2}F_{3,\downarrow}\!\left({80\over m+1}\right).
\tag{5.4}
\]

An independent subset-tree DP gives Q3 supported pairs \((0,60),(8,30),(15,16),(24,0)\), seams \(8,15,135/8\), and \(F_{3,\downarrow}(40)=F_{3,\downarrow}(80/3)=8\). Thus the \(m=1,2\) lower bounds are \(8>5\) and \(12>8\).

### 5.2 Block-Fano barrier for every \(n\ge4\)

At \(v_n\), let

\[
\kappa_{n,m}=1-\left({4(n-1)\over5n}\right)^m
+(n-1)\left[1-\left({5n-4\over5n}\right)^m\right]
=\mathbb E K_m.
\tag{5.5}
\]

Let \(k=\min(n,m)\). Conditional Fano on \(X_{Q_m}\), plus \(\ell\ge H(Z)\), gives

\[
\boxed{\ell\ge \kappa_{n,m}-H_2(e_T)-ke_T.}\tag{5.6}
\]

Every nontrivial binary prefix transcript also has \(\ell\ge1\). With \(a=m+1\),

\[
\Gamma=M_T-(3m+2)=a(\ell-1)+40e_T-m.
\tag{5.7}
\]

For \(m=2,3,4\), the entropy-conjugate identity

\[
\inf_{0\le e\le1}[-aH_2(e)+(40-ak)e]
=-a\log_2(1+2^{k-40/a})
\tag{5.8}
\]

and \(\kappa_{n,m}\ge\kappa_{4,m}\) give exact positive certificates

\[
\boxed{{16159\over102400},\quad {15561\over8000},\quad {14957\over4000}.}
\tag{5.9}
\]

For \(5\le m\le19\): if \(e_T>m/40\), (5.7) is positive. Otherwise \(e_T\le m/40<1/2\), so \(H_2(e_T)<1\), and

\[
\Gamma>
\begin{cases}
a(\kappa_{n,m}-2)-m,&40-ak\ge0,\\
a(\kappa_{n,m}-2-km/40),&40-ak<0.
\end{cases}
\tag{5.10}
\]

For fixed \(m\), once \(n\ge m\), \(k=m\) and \(\kappa_{n,m}\) increases with \(n\). It suffices to check \(4\le n\le m\le19\). The global exact minimum is

\[
\boxed{
{331725854346589385191559240189443183
\over794428636916437084448554992675781250}
\approx0.4175653279999804}
\tag{5.11}
\]

at \(n=m=19\). Thus every nontrivial tree is strictly above parity in \(M\) for \(n\ge4,2\le m\le19\).

## 6. Latency, distortion, and \(n=2\)

Joint failure contains first-answer failure, \(e_T\ge e_1\), so

\[
2L_T\ge2+2\ell+40e_1.
\tag{6.1}
\]

For \(n=3\), \(F_{3,\downarrow}(40)=8\) gives \(L_T\ge4=L_{\rm par}\). For \(n\ge4\), coordinatewise Fano gives

\[
2+2\ell+40e_1\ge
\Phi^*_{n,40}=2+2n\left[1-\log_2(1+2^{-16/n})\right].
\tag{6.2}
\]

This is nondecreasing in \(n\), and

\[
\Phi^*_{4,40}=10-8\log_2(17/16)>8
\Longleftrightarrow17^4<2\cdot16^4.
\tag{6.3}
\]

Hence \(L_T>4\) for \(n\ge4\). Equation (6.2) also closes \(m=1\): \(M_T\ge\Phi^*_{n,40}>8>5\). Always \(D_T=e_T\ge0=D_{\rm par}\).

For \(n=2\), the legal zero-error identity transcript has

\[
(M,D,L)=(3m+3,0,3).
\tag{6.4}
\]

Since \(3<4\), parity cannot dominate it for any \(m\). The full phase is empty even though the no-message memory face remains positive through \(m=14\).

## 7. Assembly, randomization, and failures

### Positive phase

- \(n=3\): (5.4) handles \(m=1,2\); (5.1)-(5.3) handle every nontrivial tree for \(3\le m\le16\); (3.4) handles the no-message leaf.
- \(n=4,5\): (6.2) handles \(m=1\); block Fano handles every nontrivial tree for \(2\le m\le18\); exact no-message signs close \(r=1\).
- \(n\ge6\): the same argument works through \(m=19\), with (3.7)-(3.8) proving the all-\(n\) no-message tail.

Conditioning on every random seed reduces a randomized policy to deterministic realizations. The bounds are affine and uniform at fixed \((n,m)\), with a strictly positive \(M\) margin, so averaging preserves strict \(M\)-dominance. This covers the randomized hull, not only trees or vertices.

### Exact failures

A fixed no-message prototype succeeds with probability at least \(2^{-n}\), so

\[
M_0-M_{\rm par}\le39-2m-{40\over2^n}.

## 2. Locked model

Let \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)\), \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}\theta\), and \(S_{1:m}\perp X\). Conditioned on all randomness, the pre-demand prefix transcript partitions \(N=2^n\) sources into \(r\) nonempty leaves \(A_j\) at depths \(d_j\), with
\[
\ell=N^{-1}\sum_j|A_j|d_j.
\]
The decoder receives no correctness oracle or source-dependent feedback. With joint success \(P_T\) and \(e_T=1-P_T\),
\[
M_T=(m+1)(1+\ell)+40e_T,
\quad L_T=1+\ell+c_{\rm comp}+20e_T,
\quad D_T=e_T,
\quad c_{\rm comp}\ge0.
\]
Dominance is weak in all coordinates with at least one strict.

## 3. No-message face and exact all-\(n\) tail

Put \(Q_m=\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}\), \(K_m=|Q_m|\).

**Occupancy projection.** Every deterministic \(r\)-leaf realization obeys
\[
\boxed{P_T\le\mathbb E_\theta\min\{1,r2^{-K_m}\}.}\tag{3.1}
\]
Indeed, conditional on \(K_m=k\), consistent answers leave at most \(2^{n-k}\) successful cube words per leaf; inconsistent repeats leave none. Across leaves at most \(\min(2^n,r2^{n-k})\) words succeed.

For \(r=1\), a fixed prototype attains
\[
\boxed{P_{0,m}(\theta)=\mathbb E2^{-K_m}=2^{-n}\sum_{B\subseteq[n]}\theta(B)^m.}\tag{3.2}
\]
This symmetric convex function is Schur-convex, so its maximum on \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\) is at \(v_n\). Write
\[
\boxed{p_{n,m}={1\over2^n(5n)^m}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}{n-1\choose k}
[(n+4+4k)^m+(4k)^m],}
\tag{3.3}
\]
\[
\boxed{G_0(n,m)=40(1-p_{n,m})-(2m+1).}\tag{3.4}
\]
For \(m\ge10\), with \(Z=\theta(B)\),
\[
p_{n,m}-p_{n,m+1}=\mathbb E[Z^m(1-Z)]
\le{m^m\over(m+1)^{m+1}}<{1\over20},
\quad\boxed{20m^m<(m+1)^{m+1}},
\tag{3.5}
\]
so \(G_0(n,m)>G_0(n,m+1)\).

## 4. Exact prefix spectrum

Let \(C_N(r)\) be minimum external path sum. Define
\[
U(s)=s(a+2)-2^{a+1},\ a=\lfloor\log_2s\rfloor,\ U(1)=0.
\]
For \(1\le d\le\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor\), set
\[
k=2^d,\quad q=\lfloor(r-1)/(k-1)\rfloor,\quad b=(r-1)-(k-1)q,
\]
\[
V_d(r)=(k-1-b)U(q)+bU(q+1).
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{C_N(1)=0,\qquad C_N(r)=\min_d[Nd+V_d(r)].}\tag{4.1}
\]
For fixed depths, place one source per leaf and all \(N-r\) extras at minimum depth \(d\). The \(2^d\) depth-\(d\) subtrees have leaf counts summing to \(r\), one equal to one. Discrete convexity of \(U\) balances the remaining counts and gives (4.1); complete subtrees attain it. Independent root-split DP agrees for all \(1\le r\le N\le64\). In particular,
\[
C_{16}=(0,16,18,21,24,28,32,36,40,45,50,53,56,60,62,64).
\]

## 6. Latency, distortion, and \(n=2\)

Since joint failure contains first-answer failure,
\[
2L_T\ge2+2\ell+40e_1.\tag{6.1}
\]
At \(n=3\), \(F_{3,\downarrow}(40)=8\) gives \(L_T\ge4\). For \(n\ge4\), coordinate Fano gives
\[
2+2\ell+40e_1\ge\Phi^*_{n,40}=2+2n[1-\log_2(1+2^{-16/n})].
\]
This is nondecreasing in \(n\), and
\[
\Phi^*_{4,40}=10-8\log_2(17/16)>8
\Longleftrightarrow17^4<2\cdot16^4.\tag{6.2}
\]
Hence \(L_T>4\) for \(n\ge4\). It also closes \(m=1\): \(M_T\ge\Phi^*_{n,40}>8>5\). Always \(D_T=e_T\ge0\).

At \(n=2\), the legal identity transcript has
\[
(M,D,L)=(3m+3,0,3).
\]
Its latency \(3<4\) kills parity for every \(m\), although the no-message memory face stays positive through \(m=14\).

- Q3: (5.3) covers \(m=1,2\); (5.1)-(5.2) every nontrivial tree for \(3\le m\le16\); §3 handles \(r=1\).

Conditioning on the full random seed reduces a randomized policy to deterministic realizations. All bounds are affine and uniform at fixed \((n,m)\), with strict positive \(M\) margin, so averaging preserves strict dominance.

A fixed no-message prototype has success at least \(2^{-n}\), hence
\[

At \(n=3,m=17\), the universal bound ties but the exact heavy-vertex gap is negative; (7.1) is negative from \(m=18\). It is negative from \(m=19\) at \(n=4,5\), and from \(m=20\) at \(n\ge6\). Together with the \(n=2\) identity this proves both directions.

let md=String.raw`# RADC Wave-7 P1 -- exact general-\(n\) sequential full-prefix phase

**W7 ID:** \(\mathrm{W7\mbox{-}SOL\mbox{-}SEQ\mbox{-}DOWN\mbox{-}STAIRCASE}\)  
**Verdict:** PROVED + independently EC-attested under the locked formal ledger.  
**Scope:** \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\), \((\rho,\lambda)=(40,20)\), sequential, every variable-length no-recovery binary prefix policy, randomized hull, joint failure distortion.

## 0. Executive theorem: 16/18/19 resolved

Let \(\Theta_n^\downarrow=\{\theta\in\Delta_{n-1}:\theta_i\ge4/(5n)\}\) and \(v_n=(n+4,4,\ldots,4)/(5n)\). The parity/complement policy has locked ledger \((M,D,L)=(3m+2,0,4)\). It dominates the complete randomized no-recovery prefix hull uniformly over \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\) exactly on
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D_n=
\begin{cases}
\varnothing,&n=2,\\
\{1,\ldots,16\},&n=3,\\
\{1,\ldots,18\},&n=4,5,\\
\{1,\ldots,19\},&n\ge6.
\end{cases}}
\]
Thus, with \(\max\varnothing=0\),
\[
\boxed{m_{\rm crit}(2)=0,\ m_{\rm crit}(3)=16,\ m_{\rm crit}(4)=m_{\rm crit}(5)=18,\ m_{\rm crit}(n)=19\ (n\ge6).}
\]
The \(n=2\) phase is empty because latency kills parity. Values 16, 18, 19 are respectively Q3, Q4/Q5, and the stable all-\(n\ge6\) cutoffs.

## 1. W7 index

| W7 ID | Statement | Tags | Ambition |
|---|---|---|---|
| W7-SOL-OCCUPANCY-PROJECTION | exact \(r\)-leaf projection/no-message moment | PI\|DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-PREFIX-SPECTRUM-N | exact \(C_N(r)\), DP checked through \(N=64\) | DR\|EC | [S] |
| W7-SOL-BLOCK-FANO-BARRIER | every nontrivial tree, \(n\ge4,2\le m\le19\) | DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-Q3-FULLPREFIX | every Q3 tree through \(m=16\) | PI\|DR\|EC | [F] |
| W7-SOL-SEQ-DOWN-STAIRCASE | complete phase | PI\|DR\|EC | [M] |
| W7-SOL-P1-ATTEST | checker in §8 | EC | [S] |

PI = inherited lock; DR = deduction; EC = exact computation; BE = bounded experiment; SB = speculative bridge. No BE/SB supports the theorem.

## 2. Model lock

Let \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)\), \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}\theta\), independent. Conditioned on all randomness, the pre-demand prefix transcript partitions \(N=2^n\) sources into \(r\) leaves \(A_j\), depths \(d_j\), and \(\ell=N^{-1}\sum_j|A_j|d_j\). With joint error \(e_T\),
\[
M_T=(m+1)(1+\ell)+40e_T,\quad L_T=1+\ell+c_{\rm comp}+20e_T,\quad D_T=e_T,\quad c_{\rm comp}\ge0.
\]
No correctness oracle/source feedback is available. Dominance is weak in all coordinates with one strict.

## 3. No-message and all-\(n\) tail

Put \(K_m=|\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}|\). For every deterministic \(r\)-leaf realization,
\[
\boxed{P_T\le\mathbb E_\theta\min\{1,r2^{-K_m}\}.}\tag{3.1}
\]
Conditional on \(K_m=k\), answers leave at most \(2^{n-k}\) compatible words per leaf, hence at most \(\min(2^n,r2^{n-k})\) successful words. For \(r=1\), a prototype attains
\[
\boxed{P_{0,m}(\theta)=\mathbb E2^{-K_m}=2^{-n}\sum_{B\subseteq[n]}\theta(B)^m.}\tag{3.2}
\]
This is symmetric convex/Schur-convex, maximized over \(\Theta_n^\downarrow\) at \(v_n\). Thus
\[
p_{n,m}={1\over2^n(5n)^m}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}{n-1\choose k}[(n+4+4k)^m+(4k)^m],
\quad G_0(n,m)=40(1-p_{n,m})-(2m+1).\tag{3.3}
\]
For \(m\ge10\),
\[
p_{n,m}-p_{n,m+1}=\mathbb E[Z^m(1-Z)]\le m^m/(m+1)^{m+1}<1/20,
\quad\boxed{20m^m<(m+1)^{m+1}},\tag{3.4}
\]
so \(G_0(n,m)>G_0(n,m+1)\).

| \(n\) | last + \(m\): exact \(G_0\) | first - \(m\): exact \(G_0\) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 16: \(845049722020265693/437893890380859375\) | 17: \(-22519522704133297/437893890380859375\) |
| 4 | 18: \(277615146191/762939453125\) | 19: \(-1227337666073/762939453125\) |
| 5 | 18: \(887975035189461090631639/582076609134674072265625\) | 19: \(-254541365995396231447867/582076609134674072265625\) |
| 6 | 19: \(2975301311635846283/19705225067138671875\) | 20: \(-2684852348710641308821/1477891880035400390625\) |

Pad \(v_n\) by zero. For every \(k\le n\),
\[
1/5+4k/(5n)>1/5+4k/[5(n+1)],\tag{3.5}
\]
so \((v_n,0)\succ v_{n+1}\), \(p_{n,m}\ge p_{n+1,m}\), and \(G_0(n,m)\le G_0(n+1,m)\). Exact \(n=6\) signs close every \(n\ge6\), not a bounded extrapolation.

## 4. Exact prefix spectrum

Let \(C_N(r)\) be minimum external path sum. Define \(U(s)=s(a+2)-2^{a+1}\), \(a=\lfloor\log_2s\rfloor\), \(U(1)=0\). For \(1\le d\le\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor\), set
\[
k=2^d,\ q=\lfloor(r-1)/(k-1)\rfloor,\ b=(r-1)-(k-1)q,\quad V_d=(k-1-b)U(q)+bU(q+1).
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{C_N(1)=0,\qquad C_N(r)=\min_d[Nd+V_d(r)].}\tag{4.1}
\]
For fixed depths, one source occupies each leaf and all \(N-r\) extras go to minimum depth \(d\). The \(2^d\) depth-\(d\) subtrees have leaf counts summing to \(r\), one equal to one. Discrete convexity of \(U\) balances the rest; complete subtrees attain the result. Root-split DP agrees for every \(1\le r\le N\le64\). In particular,
\[
C_{16}=(0,16,18,21,24,28,32,36,40,45,50,53,56,60,62,64).
\]

## 5. Every nontrivial tree

### 5.1 Q3

Set \(c_r=C_8(r)/8\), \(u_r=\mathbb E_{v_3}\min(1,r2^{-K_m})\), \(b_r=1-u_r\). Then
\[
M_T-(3m+2)\ge(m+1)c_r-(2m+1)+40b_r.\tag{5.1}
\]
The exact threshold
\[
\rho_{\rm PL}(3,m)=\max_{1\le r\le8}{[2m+1-(m+1)c_r]_+\over b_r}<40\quad(3\le m\le16)
\]
has terminal value
\[
\boxed{\rho_{\rm PL}(3,16)=144504983825683593750/3823887026147156267\approx37.790076651737.}\tag{5.2}
\]
For \(m=1,2\), \(M_T\ge[(m+1)/2]F_{3,\downarrow}(80/(m+1))\). Exact Q3 DP gives supported pairs \((0,60),(8,30),(15,16),(24,0)\), seams \(8,15,135/8\), and both required floors equal 8. Hence \(M_T\ge8>5\) and \(M_T\ge12>8\).

### 5.2 Block Fano for all \(n\ge4\)

At \(v_n\),
\[
\kappa_{n,m}=1-[4(n-1)/(5n)]^m+(n-1)[1-((5n-4)/(5n))^m]=\mathbb EK_m.
\]
With \(k=\min(n,m)\), conditional Fano on \(X_{Q_m}\) gives
\[
\boxed{\ell\ge\kappa_{n,m}-H_2(e_T)-ke_T.}\tag{5.3}
\]
A nontrivial prefix has \(\ell\ge1\). Put \(a=m+1\):
\[
\Gamma=M_T-(3m+2)=a(\ell-1)+40e_T-m.\tag{5.4}
\]
For \(m=2,3,4\), the entropy conjugate and \(\kappa_{n,m}\ge\kappa_{4,m}\) give exact positive certificates
\[
\boxed{16159/102400,\quad15561/8000,\quad14957/4000.}\tag{5.5}
\]
For \(5\le m\le19\), if \(e_T>m/40\), (5.4) is positive. Otherwise \(H_2(e_T)<1\), and
\[
\Gamma>\begin{cases}a(\kappa_{n,m}-2)-m,&40-ak\ge0,\\a(\kappa_{n,m}-2-km/40),&40-ak<0.\end{cases}\tag{5.6}
\]
Once \(n\ge m\), \(k=m\) and \(\kappa\) increases with \(n\), so checking \(4\le n\le m\le19\) suffices. The exact global minimum, at \(n=m=19\), is
\[
\boxed{331725854346589385191559240189443183/794428636916437084448554992675781250>0.}\tag{5.7}
\]
Every nontrivial tree therefore has strictly larger \(M\) for \(n\ge4,2\le m\le19\).

\[
2L_T\ge2+2\ell+40e_1.\tag{6.1}

At \(n=3\), \(F_{3,\downarrow}(40)=8\) gives \(L_T\ge4\). At \(n\ge4\), coordinate Fano gives

This is nondecreasing, and \(\Phi^*_{4,40}=10-8\log_2(17/16)>8\), equivalently \(17^4<2\cdot16^4\). Thus \(L_T>4\), and the same floor closes \(m=1\): \(M_T>8>5\). Always \(D_T=e_T\ge0\).
